title: Teach the general case first
statement: Teach the general case before a restricted one, because splitting off the restricted case and teaching it first builds a rule that later has to be undone.
detail: The curriculum BrainLift in the reading project's course plans names wrong atom boundaries as one way a curriculum graph goes wrong: splitting a restricted case from a general case, such as same-denominator before unlike-denominator fractions, makes students build predictive models that become entrenched and must be actively undone (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback1/Curriculum & Knowledge BrainLift.md`). Its prescription is to teach the most general case first and use carefully chosen examples to prevent induction of restricted rules.

evidence.quote: Splitting a restricted case from a general case (e.g., same-denominator before unlike-denominator fractions) causes students to build predictive models that become entrenched and must be actively undone.
teach the most general case first, use carefully chosen examples to prevent induction of restricted rules.
